entry.title: Take a puzzle apart, and try a piece
entry.summary: A simple puzzle can be interesting before your child can put it back together. Offer a manageable challenge and help them repeat the part they enjoy.
entry.cue: Notice whether they are lifting pieces out, turning them, or trying to fit one into the base.
detail: Davies begins with simple knob puzzles. If your child mostly removes the pieces, you can replace them so there is another chance to take them out.
When a piece becomes frustrating, offer to show a slow turn or give a small cue, then see how they continue. A harder puzzle can wait. Supervise any activity with small parts.

ageContext.bookAge: The appendix says 12–14+ months for puzzles. The pictured small-knob puzzle is from around 18 months.
ageContext.readiness: Taking pieces out can be the activity; putting them back may need adult help.
ageContext.note: Choose a simple puzzle for the part your child enjoys. The photographed small-knob example and more complex fitting are later possibilities. Age and readiness sources: The Montessori Toddler, PDF pp. 14.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
